subject: Short retention window: KV cache audit & BYOK exception routing
messages:
From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@arkera-health.com>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.com; security@redwood.com
Cc: security-team@arkera-health.com
Date: Tue, 13 Oct 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Audit evidence + short retention window for KV cache (initial ask)

Hi Soojin / Redwood security team,

Thanks again for taking a look. As discussed in our intake call, Arkera's internal policy requires us to demonstrate both audit-level access and a reproducible chain of custody for short-lived KV cache entries that hold PII-derived tokens. The key constraints we need to reconcile:

- Our retention window is 48 hours for this dataset (short-window).
- We must show: who requested the cache, request timestamp, model variant used, and a tamper-evident audit record.
- We rotate BYOK keys every 24 hours and need a plan if a customer key rotation happens mid-window.

Can you confirm what minimal audit artifacts Redwood can provide for a 48-hour window and whether we can get a signed/hashed bundle for forensic review? I'm attaching a spreadsheet that lists the fields Arkera's compliance team expects.

Attachments: arkera_artifacts_request.xlsx (list of required fields)

Appreciate a triage note and proposed next steps. If this needs an exception path, please spell out the timeline and owners.

—Liam
Liam O'Connor
Head of Security, Arkera Health
liam.oconnor@arkera-health.com

Thanks Liam — forwarding to the ops/security owners for triage. High-level ask captured.

Marcus / Priyom / Laura — please see Arkera's spreadsheet. Top-line asks we need to decide:

1) What audit events we can guarantee for 48h (token request, model id, route, response hash).
2) How we handle BYOK rotation during the short window (do we provide escrowed wrapped-keys or a signed claim?).
3) Whether this requires a documented exception in the compliance playbook and what the rollback / notification flow looks like.

Proposed next step: 30-minute sync today at 3pm PT to agree on minimal artifacts and owners. If you can't make 3pm, reply with availability.

I also want a brief internal note we can send Arkera after the sync that includes: scope, confirmed artifacts, and an estimated delivery date for the forensic bundle.

Thanks — Soojin
Soojin Lee
Head of Security Programs, Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Cc: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@arkera-health.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Oct 2026 13:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Audit evidence + short retention window for KV cache (initial ask)

Quick technical triage notes ahead of the 3pm sync. I sketched a minimal approach we can deliver within Arkera's timeline. Attachment: kvcache-retention-proposal.pdf (short tech note).

Summary of constraints / proposal:
- Audit events we can emit in 48h: request_id, user_id (hashed), timestamp (UTC), model_id, route, node_id, and a CRC32/sha256 of the returned output. We can also export KV cache metadata (key id, TTL, created_at) to a secure object store for the retention window.
- BYOK rotation: when a customer key rotates, Redwood cannot decrypt prior wrapped keys without the customer's re-wrapping or an escrow token. Options:
  A) Customer provides a short-lived escrow token (recommended for Arkera) that allows us to unwrap and create signed archive bundles at the time of rotation.
  B) We keep an encrypted, HSM-wrapped key envelope for 72h (requires exception to default lifecycle) so we can produce proofs if rotation happens mid-window.
- For tamper evidence: sign the audit bundle with our infra signing key + include per-entry sha256 digests. We can timestamp-sign the bundle via an internal CA and provide the signature artifact.

Open questions for the sync:
- Does Arkera need raw outputs or only hashes? (hashes reduce PII exposure)
- Is Arkera comfortable with an escrow token flow (they control the escrow lifetime)?
- Do we need SLAed delivery for the bundle (e.g., 48h post-request for forensic export)?

I'll walk through the PDF at 3pm and mark the small changes required in infra (Priyom) to enable automatic bundle creation + short-term escrow.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@arkera-health.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Oct 2026 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Audit evidence + short retention window for KV cache (initial ask)

Good sync — summary and action items below (pulling from the meeting notes: sec-qa-notes-20261013.md).

Decisions made:
- Minimum artifact: request_id, model_id, node_id, timestamp, output_hash (sha256), kv_meta (key_id, ttl, created_at). We will provide hashes instead of raw outputs by default; raw outputs can be provided under a documented exception.
- BYOK rotation: Arkera to provide an escrow token for any planned key rotation during a 48h window. For emergency rotations, we will request a signed unlock from Arkera security.
- Tamper-evidence: Redwood infra will generate a timestamped bundle signed with infra signing key; bundle stored in S3 with 60-day access logs for customers under an evidence path. (Note: 60-day access logs is an internal policy exception and requires CISO sign-off.)

Owners & timeline:
- Marcus: finalize the bundle schema + signature format by 2026-10-20. (JIRA SEC-4123)
- Priyom: implement short-term escrow envelope workflow and S3 evidence path by 2026-11-03.
- Laura: draft the customer-facing exception doc and procurement checklist; send to Arkera by 2026-10-22.

Deliverables to Arkera:
1) A one-page triage summary (scope, artifacts, exception path) — Laura to send (due 2026-10-22).
2) Example signed bundle sample (hash-only) — Marcus to deliver by 2026-10-20.

Next steps: Laura will send the triage summary to Arkera with the proposed timeline and include a request that Arkera confirm their escrow process. I've created SEC-4123 and linked the drive doc: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1KVCacheProposal.

Priyom
Priyom Das
Principal Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference
